description: Environmental crises are borne of environmental histories. In this class, we examine how we arrived at the present through long histories of human and non-human relationships that span rare earth mineral extraction to swampy-earthed resistance to early settler colonizers.  We will utilize the resources like the college archives and Natural Lands, and look at the specificity of Midwestern environmental histories as well as planetary processes. Students will learn how to read a landscape and historicize how processes like colonization, industrialization, suburban development and contamination have shaped the environment.
